newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court urged to jail paedophile case suspects.
newsitem.headline: Paris court urged to jail paedophile case suspects.

text.p: A French state prosecutor asked a court on Monday to jail three main suspects in a paedophilia trial involving 71 men accused of organising or subscribing to a network selling pornographic films featuring boys.

Prosecutor Michele Ghanassia asked the court to sentence Jean-Manuel Vuillaume, 45, to three years in prison, with another two years suspended. He is accused of filming seven paedophile videos entitled "Toro Bravo", which were sold by the hundreds in France in 1994.
Vuillaume denies having shot the videos. Investigators have said that the videos were filmed in Colombia in a homosexual brothel owned by Vuillaume.

The prosecutor asked for the same sentence for Miguel Caignet, 42, a neo-Nazi accused of selling the videos, and a sentence of one year, with another two years suspended, for Michel Meigniez, 42, who was alleged to have helped to sell the videos.
She also sought heavy fines against the three men, who said they did not know that the actors in the films were underaged.
"This case does not put paedophilia or homosexuality on trial" but simply targets "a network of delinquants who have made a business out of exploiting minors", Ghanassia said.
She requested suspended sentences or fines for the 68 other defendants.

The two-week-old trial coincided with a French police swoop in which hundreds of suspected clients of a network seelling paedophile videos were questioned and more than 200 formally placed under investigation. The crackdown started a controversy after five of those targetted committed suicide.
